note_en: 比起A，B更… sets up a comparison where English would say "compared with A" or "rather than A": 比起干巴巴地讲道理，孩子们更愿意相信一只认真负责的公鸡 "rather than dry lectures, children would sooner believe a conscientious rooster." The thing being outdone comes first, after 比起, and the main clause usually contains 更 or 才. The text uses it twice; compare 比起…自己，阿黄才是真正值得尊敬的"劳动模范".
